newsitem.title: USA: Singer to exit U.S. furniture manufacturing.
newsitem.headline: Singer to exit U.S. furniture manufacturing.

text.p: Singer Co said Friday it would exit the U.S. furniture manufacturing business.
It did not say if it would take any charges for the move. Officials at Singer were not available for comment.

Singer said its U.S. furniture business suffered from a declining market share and considerable excess manufacturing capacity. It said it closed two of its three U.S. furniture making plants in late 1996 and is initiating talks to sell the remaining plant.
Singer made the announcement in reporting a 1996 fourth quarter loss of $0.39 per share. It cited a loss of $16.5 million related to inefficiencies in the downsizing of its furniture making business.
Later, a Singer spokesman said the company would record no further costs for the furniture business, which had about $20 million of Singer's $1.2 billion of revenues in 1996.

He said Singer would continue making furniture in Latin America and Asia. Singer derives about 47 percent of its annual sales from home electronics and other home items, and furniture manufacturing is included in this segment, the spokesman said.
